tools.name: guardian_request_upload
tools.description:
Get a pre-signed URL for uploading a large CSV (more than ~200 rows).

Use this instead of pasting rows into ``guardian_review``. Returns ``upload_url``,
``dataset_id`` and a ready-to-run ``curl`` command: run it (replace ``data.csv``
with your file; gzip is accepted with ``Content-Encoding: gzip``)

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "guardian_review" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "guardian_review" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload · Private data: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload · Public sink: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload · Destructive: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload · Private data: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload · Public sink: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload · Destructive: guardian_review, guardian_request_upload

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "guardian_review" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
